recomputed: All 13 SOURCES.tsv entries matched their SHA-256 and size (2,769,331 bytes total). I parsed the eight publisher workbooks and the GEO workbook through their final rows and verified archive CRCs, the paper XML, the 20-sample GEO SOFT and ENA records, and the BioStudies supplement inventory. Fresh publisher S4 and S7 downloads matched the saved bytes. All ten repository fingerprints in comparison.json matched. The five authored ledgers contain a manual, verification and comparability record for this dataset, with no additional comparison spec or concordance review. The existing direct comparison already uses the 43 public pairs. The registry and provenance specify pure Iberian minus crossbred, adjusted for sex, on log2(GEO-described normalized expression + 1). The manuscript and Table 2 define the opposite author orientation (33 S4 genes higher in crossbreds, 18 in pure Iberians). GEO has five animals in each breed-by-sex cell. The article excludes one male pure Iberian. Full-rank fits of the 51 pooled and 158 male-only base means give HT125IBM (GSM6062950, SRX14985618, SRR18907611) SVD weights of −1.86e-16 and −1.53e-16. Independent QR gives −2.18e-16 and −2.44e-17. The minimum other pooled weight is 0.0400097. With the five eligible males omitted in turn, only HT125IBM reproduces the 51 S4 base means under median-of-ratios normalization (maximum relative error 4.22e-15, versus 0.07746–0.11159 for the other four). All 15,629 published expression profiles match their GEO row within 4.98e-14. Of 19,471 fitted features, 14,306 have public DE rows. Eight S4 IDs are fitted but lack public symbols. The 43/51 public pairs (84.31%) give 43/43 matching signs, Pearson 0.971947962, Spearman 0.991543340, median absolute effect difference 0.129947443 and maximum 0.925408972. S4 reports all 51 at BH < 0.1 and |log2FC| ≥ log2(1.2). Registered calls are HROB and MIR150-1, with HROB alone shared. At raw P < 0.05 the paired author/local/shared counts are 43/34/34 and at BH < 0.05 they are 27/1/1. Outside S4 there are 840 raw-P and one BH registered calls at 0.05. S7 Global gives 5/5 matching signs using S2 IDs, with three genes also in S4. Its P values test assay correlation. I reran all four models from newly extracted workbook inputs using the pinned R 4.6.2, limma 3.68.5 and DESeq2 1.52.0. All 204 selected-model rows and 99 positive-call rows matched the saved results. Maximum 20-animal limma replay errors were 3.79e-14 for logFC, 2.31e-13 for t, 1.35e-13 for P and 1.40e-13 for BH. The 19-animal limma fit calls five genes, four publicly mapped, with three S4 hits including two publicly mapped. Genotype-only and sex-adjusted DESeq2 recover 49 and 43 S4 calls, respectively, with 51/51 matching signs and zero called genes outside S4. CNOT8 and WFIKKN1 have genotype-only BH 0.10501885 versus S4 BH 0.08881274. The source-defined orientation, threshold and complete S4 list support the selected-results closure. Reference coverage falls below the v2 minimum and the cohorts differ.
problems: S7 Global contains qualitative significance information that the proposal missed. Its caption assigns significance to bold RNA-seq effects. GRPEL2 and UQCRC2 are bold and absent from S4. TBCD is unbolded despite S4 BH 2.48e-7. GRPEL2’s displayed |log2FC| of 0.212 is itself below log2(1.2). S7 supplies no numeric DE P or BH that could reconcile these labels. The corrected proposal keeps review_required and unresolved for this conflict while retaining compared for the completed S4 comparison.

The manual summary makes HROB sound like the only registered gene meeting the paper’s rule. The full public table has two, HROB and MIR150-1. Only HROB belongs to S4. The 19-animal limma analysis also does not retain two publicly mapped S4 hits from the 20-animal fit. It retains HROB and adds CENPF.

The successful DESeq2 call counts include genes without public registered symbols, and filtered genes lack adjusted P values. Of the 49 and 43 reconstructed calls, 42 and 35 respectively have public symbols. The corrected proposal gives these denominators and limits the call comparison to available statistics.
